{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire op_add = (Oper == 3'b000);
    wire op_ab  = (Oper == 3'b001);
    wire op_ba  = (Oper == 3'b010);
    wire op_or  = (Oper == 3'b011);
    wire op_and = (Oper == 3'b100);
    wire op_xor = (Oper == 3'b101);
    wire op_xnor = (Oper == 3'b110);
    wire arithmetic_enable = op_add | op_ab | op_ba;
    wire carry_in = op_ab | op_ba;

    // Share one arithmetic network. Complement the subtrahend.
    wire [63:0] x = a ^ {64{op_ba}};
    wire [63:0] y = b ^ {64{op_ab}};
    wire [63:0] p = x ^ y;
    wire [63:0] g = x & y;

    // Four-bit groups, followed by a sixteen-group parallel prefix.
    wire [15:0] group_p [0:4];
    wire [15:0] group_g [0:4];
    wire [15:0] group_carry;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result;

    genvar k, s, j;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : make_groups
            assign group_p[0][k] = &p[4*k +: 4];
            assign group_g[0][k] = g[4*k+3]
                | (p[4*k+3] & g[4*k+2])
                | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]);
        end
        for (s = 0; s < 4; s = s + 1) begin : prefix_stage
            for (j = 0; j < 16; j = j + 1) begin : prefix_column
                if (j >= (1 << s)) begin : combine
                    assign group_g[s+1][j] = group_g[s][j]
                        | (group_p[s][j] & group_g[s][j-(1 << s)]);
                    assign group_p[s+1][j] = group_p[s][j]
                        & group_p[s][j-(1 << s)];
                end else begin : pass_through
                    assign group_g[s+1][j] = group_g[s][j];
                    assign group_p[s+1][j] = group_p[s][j];
                end
            end
        end
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : finish_groups
            wire [3:0] c;
            if (k == 0) begin : first_group
                assign group_carry[k] = carry_in;
            end else begin : other_group
                assign group_carry[k] = group_g[4][k-1]
                    | (group_p[4][k-1] & carry_in);
            end
            assign c[0] = group_carry[k];
            assign c[1] = g[4*k] | (p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign c[2] = g[4*k+1]
                | (p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                | (p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign c[3] = g[4*k+2]
                | (p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & c[0]);
            assign arithmetic_result[4*k +: 4] = p[4*k +: 4] ^ c;
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        sum = ({64{arithmetic_enable}} & arithmetic_result)
            | ({64{op_or}} & (a | b))
            | ({64{op_and}} & (a & b))
            | ({64{op_xor}} & (a ^ b))
            | ({64{op_xnor}} & (a ~^ b));
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The suspected bottleneck is a mapped arithmetic carry path followed by operation selection, potentially including operation-control distribution. Available evidence is limited to the RTL's three 64-bit arithmetic alternatives; no mapped netlist, critical-path report, or baseline arrival time was supplied. This does not establish three independent mapped adders or any serial-adder chain: Yosys can restructure the arithmetic. The actual bottleneck must be established from the fixed-flow timing report.",
  "rewrite": "Use one shared modulo-2^64 arithmetic network: a+b for 000, a+~b+1 for 001, and ~a+b+1 for 010. Implement carries with four-bit lookahead groups and a four-stage parallel-prefix network across the sixteen groups, followed by local lookahead and sum XORs. Use mutually exclusive decoded masks to combine arithmetic and logical results. No final carry is computed because it is not observable.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis, not a measurement: bounded-depth group-prefix carry computation may shorten the maximum arithmetic data path relative to the baseline mapping, while arithmetic sharing may reduce output-selection complexity. No numerical gain is supportable without running the specified flow. Operand-conditioning XORs, decoded-control fanout, and ABC restructuring could offset the benefit or make this candidate slower.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Sharing arithmetic is intended to offset the prefix network, operand-conditioning XORs, and buffering costs. Prefix logic can consume more area than a compact carry implementation. Compliance with the 13098.437440 um^2 mapped-area cap is unverified. No EDA tools were available here: this is one candidate for evaluation, not a claimed eligible result. Acceptance requires full functional equivalence, mapped area at or below the cap, and zero max-slew/max-capacitance violations under the exact specified Yosys/ABC/OpenSTA flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, and combinational interface are unchanged. For all binary 64-bit a and b values, operations 000 through 110 implement add, a-b, b-a, OR, AND, XOR, and XNOR respectively; 111 produces zero. Subtraction identities and discarded overflow preserve arithmetic modulo 2^64. The original internal c_out has no observable output and is omitted. No clocks, state, input restrictions, assumptions, or don't-cares are introduced. These identities justify the construction but do not replace the required tool-based equivalence check."
}
